tools.name: session_brief
tools.description: Stack changes since your last cursor (retired models, prices, packages, picks). Send provider, model and package ids (never a manifest) plus that cursor. Returns clear|changed|attention, ≤3 sourced actions, a new cursor. First pick: decide. Live API error: rescue. Quotes/compare/audit/freshness/outc

tools.name: rescue
tools.description: Live API errors: paste the exact error (429, 402, 529, insufficient_quota, model_not_found) and provider id. Returns cause, fix and fallback, or checks to run. First pick: decide. Stack changes since last cursor: session_brief. Quotes/compare/audit/freshness/outcomes: depot.

tools.name: decide
tools.description: First pick, no API key needed, before writing integration code (LLM, sandbox, vector DB, search, email, Postgres, auth, browser, observability). First call: set a stable clientInfo.name (e.g. acme-support-agent), then {task:'run untrusted Python in a sandbox'}. Returns the dated Depot Pick, runner-u

tools.name: depot
tools.description: Catalog reads and outcome reports: quotes, compare, audit, freshness. Use for those and to report an outcome. Not for a first pick (decide), a live API error (rescue), or stack changes since your last cursor (session_brief). Only report_outcome writes state; every other op is a read. Ops: prices: qu

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "session_brief" stacks urgency/override words (never, attention). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: rescue, decide.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: rescue, decide

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
